content: Firebase official docs (fetched 2026-08-06): web/JS SDK offline persistence uses persistentLocalCache with persistentSingleTabManager as default when no tab manager specified; persistentMultipleTabManager is IndexedDB multi-tab (web). initializeFirestore must set localCache at creation; cacheSizeBytes configurable (min 1MB); default web cache threshold ~10% of available storage with automatic eviction of unused docs. React Native persistence is backed by AsyncStorage (@react-native-async-storage/async-storage); @firebase/firestore ships a dedicated react-native export (dist/index.rn.js, verified on npm registry 4.17.0). Offline: queries run only against cached docs; disableNetwork/enableNetwork control the queue. Cache is NOT cleared between sessions — data persists across app reloads in Expo Go. AsyncStorage Android default SQLite cap is 6MB (community-documented, configurable via AsyncStorage_db_size_in_MB) — orders of magnitude above this app's needs but worth knowing.
